title: "Informazione" for Giovanni Noceto: a full page of figure cipher annexed to his letter to Francesco Campana, May 1537, bare
correspondents: Giovanni Noceto (Bagnone, Lunigiana) -> Francesco Campana, first secretary of Cosimo I
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo del Principato 331, cc. 70-71
folio_note: c. 70r: Noceto's clear covering letter to Campana (Bagnone, 2 May 1537); c. 71r: about 25 lines of continuous figures, no clear word; versos blank. Inventory vol. I p. 30: c. 70 "In allegato c. 71"; c. 71 "Informazione [per Giovanni Noceto], [1537]", note "Cifra allegata a c. 70".
status: Bare: no gloss on c. 71r; c. 70 is the covering letter and c. 72 an unrelated letter (Annibale da Napoli, Mantua). Seen at 900 px.
why: The earliest cipher piece found in the Carteggio universale (first year of Cosimo I), a self-contained page from the Lunigiana frontier, unread.
verify: Transcribe c. 71r at full size; test two-figure grouping; look for Noceto/Campana keys in ASF Cifrari II serie.

title: Gerolamo del Vezzo and Niccolò Campana: the Medici intelligence correspondence from Modena, Piacenza and Bologna, 1539-1541, with figure runs and letter-pair codes, bare
correspondents: Gerolamo del Vezzo (secretary of Lucrezia Pico Rangoni, Modena; writing as from "Barzalona") -> Lorenzo Pagni and Niccolò Campana (Bologna) -> Lorenzo Pagni, secretary of Cosimo I
language: Italian (figure groups and letter-pair codes such as EE, DD, KK, ZZ in clear text)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo del Principato 337, c. 330; 347, c. 597; 349, c. 42; 353, c. 337
folio_note: 337 c. 330r-v (del Vezzo, "Barzalona" = Modena, 20 Dec 1539, to [Lorenzo Pagni], annexed to Campana's c. 335): a full page with many figure runs and code pairs (EE, DD, KK, &&); 347 c. 597 (Campana, Bologna, 22 Nov 1540, to Pagni): two figure passages; 349 c. 42 (del Vezzo, Piacenza, 4 Feb 1541, to Campana, annexed to c. 12): six figure runs; 353 c. 337 (del Vezzo, "Barzalona", 27 Aug 1540, to Campana): mostly clear with codes ZZ, KK, HS and one figure run. Inventory vol. I pp. 112, 209, 224, 279 note each "Parzialmente in cifra" (with "luogo di emissione: Barzalona" for 337 and 353). The same network's June 1542 pieces (357 c. 558 "Cifra", an avviso of Bernardino Duretti; c. 564 del Vezzo "In codice") are in 357 parte II, which PAD lists without images.
status: Bare on all four: no interlinear or marginal decipherment; the adjacent carte (337 cc. 329, 331, 335; 347 cc. 596, 598; 349 cc. 41, 43, 12; 353 cc. 336, 338) are clear letters of the network, none a decipherment.
why: A cover-name intelligence network run by Cosimo I's secretaries into Farnese and Este territory (1539-42), with a shared figure code: several letters for one system, unread.
verify: Transcribe the four letters; build the figure-group inventory; the clear context names many persons (Farnese, Rangoni, the "Marchese"), useful as cribs; check 357 parte II at ASF.

title: Copy of a cipher letter of Cardinal Alessandro Farnese (to Pier Luigi Farnese), intercepted, August 1547: a full page of figures, bare
correspondents: Cardinal Alessandro Farnese -> [Pier Luigi Farnese, duke of Parma and Piacenza] (copy made in Cosimo I's chancery)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo del Principato 384, c. 78
folio_note: c. 78r headed "Copia / D'una littera del card.le Farnese", then about 35 lines of continuous figures, a few clear words at the foot. Inventory vol. III p. 103: "(Alessandro Farnese) a (Pier Luigi Farnese), s.l., s.d., c. 78", note "Copia di una lettera in cifra".
status: Bare (checked at 2000 px). Its neighbours are glossed: c. 70 (Valerio Amanio to Pier Luigi Farnese, Venice) has its decipherment at c. 71 ("Deciferato di M. Valerio"), and c. 76 (copy of a chapter of the French ambassador's letter, Rome 10 Aug 1547) has its decipherment at c. 79 (same heading); c. 78 has none (c. 80 is an unrelated letter).
why: An intercepted Farnese cipher of the weeks before Pier Luigi's murder (Sept 1547), unread; a Farnese family key of 1541-42 is already worked in this repo (targets/vatican5), and the glossed Amanio and French-ambassador copies in the same gathering show the chancery was reading Farnese traffic.
verify: Transcribe; test against the vatican5 Farnese key family; read cc. 70-71 and 76-79 to see which systems the chancery had broken.
